opening: We build our HTTP, QUIC, DNS and HTML tooling with golang.org/x/net (current master) on the Go 1.27 toolchain and found five problems: our HTTP/2 servers set up with the http2 package stopped offering HTTP/2, our DNS code accepts and writes malformed SVCB records, the html package can render a parsed document into markup that runs a script, QUIC streams return corrupted data after retransmissions, and XSRF tokens collide. All of them reproduce with the packages' public API.

requirements.m01: A QUIC stream returns corrupted data when the peer resends stream data that overlaps data we already received but have not read yet, as happens on retransmission: the overlapping part is written into the stream's buffer again instead of being dropped, so Read returns bytes in the wrong place or repeated, and the connection can fail with a FINAL_SIZE_ERROR. Data received again, in whole or in part, must be deduplicated: reading the stream must give each byte exactly once in order, followed by io.EOF after the final frame, whether the earlier data was still buffered or already read.
requirements.m02: http2.ConfigureServer no longer prepares the server's TLS settings. When we call it on an http.Server and then serve TLS through a listener built from that server's TLSConfig (for example tls.Listen, or an httptest server with ts.TLS = ts.Config.TLSConfig before StartTLS), only http/1.1 is offered and HTTP/2 clients fail the handshake with "tls: no application protocol". After ConfigureServer, the server's TLSConfig must never be nil, and its NextProtos must contain both "h2" and "http/1.1": for a server with no TLSConfig, with an empty one, and with one that already lists only "http/1.1" or only "h2" (keep the existing entry and add the missing one). A client whose transport is set up with http2.ConfigureTransport or http2.ConfigureTransports (for example one with its own TLSClientConfig and InsecureSkipVerify) must then reach such a server over HTTP/2: the response's ProtoMajor is 2.
requirements.m03: Building and parsing SVCB and HTTPS records does not enforce that a record's service parameters come in strictly increasing key order with no key repeated. A Builder accepts an SVCBResource or HTTPSResource whose Params list port (key 3) before alpn (key 1), or alpn twice, and writes a record other resolvers reject; a Parser accepts a response whose SVCB record lists its parameters as key 2 then key 1, or key 1 twice. Both must fail: Builder.SVCBResource and Builder.HTTPSResource must return an error for parameters that are out of order or repeated, and parsing such a record must return an error. Records with parameters in increasing key order keep working, and a parameter value longer than 65535 bytes is still refused.
requirements.m04: xsrftoken.Generate gives the same token for different user and action pairs when one of them starts or ends with a colon: user "foo:" with action "wah" and user "foo" with action ":wah" get identical tokens when generated at the same moment, so a token issued for one action is accepted for the other. Tokens for different (user, action) pairs must always differ, and tokens must still be accepted by Valid for the user and action they were generated for.
